prompt:
A configured catalog can drift from recorded lockfile specifiers while frozen installation and dependency-status checking still accept stale state. Make catalog consistency checks work across the affected production APIs and consumers. Changes or removal of recorded specifiers must be detected. Unchanged catalogs and newly added unused entries must remain accepted, unrelated lockfile checks must keep working, and rejection of a frozen installation must preserve lockfile bytes. Dependencies and project configuration are already prepared. Change only existing production TypeScript source. Run the supplied validation before and after the repair.

Before investigating implementation, run the supplied native validation command: npm run test:typelatch-benchmark. After making the requested change, run it again. Only existing production source may change. Keep tests, dependencies, manifests and configuration fixed. Generated compiler outputs may be rebuilt.

For your first task-directed investigation, obtain relevant evidence through the advertised repository provider when present, otherwise through native tools. Provider startup instructions and harmless top-level metadata checks are separate. Then choose freely among all available tools. Native compiler, language service, package-manager filters and source reads are available in every condition. Prefer concise evidence and avoid redundant reads. Do not mistake package reachability for proven symbol impact or an incomplete result for absence.

Stay inside this project. Do not use the network, install packages, inspect repository history, read external files or delegate work. Supplied native validation commands may execute their configured external runner, but do not inspect that runner or other external files. Native source, installed declarations and project configuration inside the workspace remain available.
